q: Electrical energy is energy associated with the flow of charge through any part of circuit.
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. Energy associated with the flow of charge through any part of circuit.

q: Electrical energy can be generated from source of emf such as batteries, generators, dynamos and photovoltaic cells.
e: True. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. From source of emf such as batteries, generators, dynamos and photovoltaic cells.

q: Electrical energy can be stored in other forms for future application using fuel cells, batteries, capacitors and inductors.
e: True. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. Other forms for future application using fuel cells, batteries, capacitors and inductors.

q: The work done $W$ in bringing the amount of charge $Q$ from A to B is $W = Q/V$.
e: False. The right claim is this: By the definition of potential difference, the work done in bringing a unit positive charge from A to B is V. Potential difference is the electrical push between two points; no push, no current. The printed line wrongly says the work done W in bringing the amount of charge Q from A to B is W = Q/V.

q: The work done $W$ by the battery in taking the charge $Q$ from A to B is the electrical energy supplied by the battery.
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. From A to B is the electrical energy supplied by the battery.

q: The electrical energy supplied by the battery is transformed into heat energy in the resistor $R$.
e: True. Resistance opposes current and turns electrical energy into heat. By the battery is transformed into heat energy in the resistor R.

q: Heat energy is produced because protons collide with the atoms in the resistor $R$ when they pass through it.
e: False. The right claim is this: Heat energy is produced because the electrons collide with the atoms in the resistor R when they pass through it. In metals the mobile carriers are electrons, drifting opposite the conventional-current arrow. The printed line wrongly says heat energy is produced because protons collide with the atoms in the resistor R when they pass through it.

q: The electrical energy $W$ produced by the battery is $W = VIt$.
e: True. A battery converts chemical energy into electrical energy and holds a pd at its terminals. The relation in this line is W = VIt.

q: The electrical energy $W$ can also be written as $W = I^2Rt$.
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. The relation in this line is W = I^2Rt.

q: The electrical energy $W$ can also be written as $W = V^2 R t$.
e: False. The right claim is this: The electrical energy W can also be written as W=(V^2)/(R)t. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. The printed line wrongly says the electrical energy W can also be written as W = V^2 R t.

q: If an electric motor is connected between A and B, the electrical energy will be transformed into mechanical energy.
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. A and B, the electrical energy will be transformed into mechanical energy.

q: The practical unit of electrical energy is kilowatt hour ($kWh$).
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. The practical unit of electrical energy is kilowatt hour (kWh).

q: $1 	ext{ kWh}$ is equal to $3.60 	imes 10^3 	ext{ J}$.
e: False. The right claim is this: 1 kWh is equal to 1000 W × 1 h, which is 3. 60 × 10^6 J. The printed line wrongly says 1 ext kWh is equal to 3.

q: $1 	ext{ kWh} = 1000 	ext{ W} 	imes 1 	ext{ h} = 1000 	imes 60 	imes 60 	ext{ J}$.
e: True. 1 ext kWh = 1000 ext W imes 1 ext h = 1000 imes 60 imes 60 ext J. The relation in this line is kWh = 1000 ext W imes 1 ext h.

q: Electrical power is the total amount of electrical energy transferred.
e: False. The right claim is this: If the electrical energy W is transferred in the time t, then the electrical power P is P=(W)/(t). Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. The printed line wrongly says electrical power is the total amount of electrical energy transferred.

q: If the electrical energy $W$ is transferred in the time $t$, then the electrical power $P$ is $P = W/t$.
e: True. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. The relation in this line is P = W/t.

q: The electrical power $P$ can be calculated as $P = VI$.
e: True. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. The relation in this line is P = VI.

q: The electrical power $P$ can be calculated as $P = I^2/R$.
e: False. The right claim is this: The electrical power P can be calculated as P = VI. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. The printed line wrongly says the electrical power P can be calculated as P = I^2/R.

q: The unit of electrical power $P$ is the watt ($W$).
e: True. Electrical power is the energy transfer rate, P = VI, also I^2R or V^2/R. The unit of electrical power P is the watt (W).

q: If $1 	ext{ joule (J)}$ of electrical energy is transferred in $1 	ext{ second (s)}$ the electrical power is $1 	ext{ watt (W)}$.
e: True. Electrical energy is what a current carries through a circuit, later turned into heat, light or motion. 1 ext second (s) the electrical power is 1 ext watt (W).
